covered_report_window: U.S.-listed companies reporting after the Wednesday, September 16, 2026 U.S. market close and before the Thursday, September 17, 2026 U.S. market open
market_context_summary: The Federal Reserve decision and press conference occur immediately before Lennar reports. Markets expect a rate hike; the 10-year Treasury yield was near 5%, and 30-year mortgage rates were near a 14-month high, creating unusually high macro sensitivity for a homebuilder.

exclusions.reason: Small, thinly covered issuer; insufficient evidence quality.
Company IR schedules Q3 results for September 29, not September 17.
Company IR confirms September 22 before open.
September 17 timing is estimated, not company-confirmed.
Company had not officially announced Q2 results timing after stating timing would be announced later.

ranked_companies.timing: After market close Wednesday, September 16, 2026; company-confirmed
ranked_companies.expected_driver: New orders and home-sale gross margin; Q4 margin/order outlook
ranked_companies.key_risk_to_call: Low valuation, de-risked price, and short-covering relief
ranked_companies.pass_agreement: 2 Lean Down, 1 Neutral; material category disagreement
ranked_companies.method_update_note: Existing expectation-bar and forward-look checks applied; no new method change
ranked_companies.one_sentence_thesis: High mortgage rates, falling order expectations, and fragile margins favor a downside reaction unless Lennar clears a low bar and provides credible sequential margin recovery.
ranked_companies.market_expectation_summary: Consensus is about $1.29-$1.30 EPS and $8.4 billion revenue; management guided to 21,000-22,000 orders, 20,500-21,500 deliveries, $375,000-$380,000 average selling price, and about 16% home-sale gross margin.
ranked_companies.upside_case_summary: Orders reach the upper end, gross margin meets or exceeds 16%, and Q4 commentary shows incentives and costs easing.
ranked_companies.downside_case_summary: Orders miss, incentives remain heavy, or Q4 margin/order commentary weakens after the Fed/rate shock.
ranked_companies.options_or_positioning_summary: Options price roughly 6.3%-7.3%, above the 4.4% historical average realized move; short interest was about 8.4% of float with 7.4 days to cover.
ranked_companies.analyst_revision_summary: The EPS consensus slipped to $1.29 from $1.31 in the final week; UBS expected an in-line print but potentially weak orders, while Bank of America maintained Underperform and cut its target to $70.

excluded_high_reversal_or_weak_names.reason: Absolute score qualifies, but consensus reversal risk of 46 exceeds the 40 cutoff and pass disparity is material.

research_allocation_view.plain_statement: This is a research prioritization model, not financial advice.

consensus_method.disparity_definition: 0-100 composite of dispersion in the three direction scores and reversal-risk estimates; lower means tighter independent agreement.
consensus_method.learned_lessons_review: The existing mandatory expectation-bar, decisive-metric, forward-look, and separate reversal-risk controls were applied. No new method change was warranted.

detailed_company_sections.consensus_summary: Passes A and B leaned down on order risk, mortgage affordability, and margin fragility. Pass C stayed Neutral because the share price and valuation are de-risked and short interest can amplify relief.
detailed_company_sections.pass_agreement_pattern: Pass A -46 / 36 risk; Pass B -56 / 43 risk; Pass C -24 / 58 risk. Two Lean Down, one Neutral.
detailed_company_sections.thesis: The decisive metric is new orders, with home-sale gross margin and the Q4 outlook as the forward override.
detailed_company_sections.expectation_summary: Street EPS near $1.29-$1.30 and revenue near $8.4 billion; management's Q3 targets include 21,000-22,000 orders and about 16% gross margin.
detailed_company_sections.upside_case: Orders and margin meet the high end while management signals less incentive pressure and continued cash generation.
detailed_company_sections.downside_case: Orders fall below guidance and the forward margin bridge weakens as mortgage rates approach 7%.
detailed_company_sections.reversal_risk_assessment: Moderate at 46. The stock trades near 0.9x book after a large decline, published expectations have fallen, and elevated short interest could turn an in-line quarter into a relief rally.
detailed_company_sections.sentiment_read: Retail discussion is limited and mostly focused on rates, book value, incentives, and the 16% margin target. No reliable 7/14/30-day social trend was strong enough to affect the score.
detailed_company_sections.positioning_read: The implied move is about 6.3%-7.3%, richer than the 4.4% historical average realized earnings move. Short interest of about 8.4% of float creates two-sided gap risk.
detailed_company_sections.analyst_revision_read: Final-week EPS estimates moved lower; UBS was Neutral and worried orders could miss, while Bank of America maintained Underperform and cut its target.
detailed_company_sections.base_case: A near-consensus quarter with soft orders and cautious Q4 commentary produces a modest decline, likely inside the implied move.
detailed_company_sections.bull_case: A clean 16%+ margin, upper-end orders, and better Q4 incentives trigger a short-covering rally.
detailed_company_sections.bear_case: Order weakness and a weaker margin/outlook compound the Fed-driven affordability shock, producing a move beyond the implied range.
detailed_company_sections.final_directional_judgment: Lean Down, but the expected magnitude does not clearly exceed the options-implied move.
detailed_company_sections.allocation_priority_note: Not prioritized because reversal risk exceeds 40 and one pass was Neutral; 100% remains unallocated.
detailed_company_sections.disparity_impact_note: Moderate disparity reduced confidence from what the raw bearish average alone might imply.
detailed_company_sections.method_update_note: Repeated expectation-bar and forward-look lessons were applied; no new calibration rule was added.

disclaimer_text: This is research, not financial advice. Earnings reactions are highly uncertain and can be driven by market positioning, guidance, macro conditions, and management commentary rather than reported results alone.
